Both fixes are correctly done, not just present. Going further than the brief asked: the round-2 diff turned out to touch three additional passages that round 1's adsense critic had flagged as hard-rule violations (a fabricated File.Replace quote, a bracket-substituted word in the ext4 journal quote, and an overstated File.Move claim framed as the documentation's own words) — these weren't in my assigned brief, but since they're part of the same commit and load-bearing for a pass/fail call, I re-verified all three against live sources rather than assuming they were fixed correctly. All three check out: the journal.html page's actual sentence is 'Should the system crash during the second slow write, the journal can be replayed all the way to the latest commit record, guaranteeing the atomicity of whatever gets written through the journal to the disk' — the article now quotes 'slow' verbatim instead of the invented '[real]'. File.Move's live Remarks section states verbatim, 'Moving the file across disk volumes is equivalent to copying the file and deleting it from the source if the copying was successful' — the article now quotes this in full (previously truncated and wrapped in an unsupported 'a same-volume move is a single filesystem operation' framing) and separately, honestly, states in its own words that the documentation 'says nothing directly about the same-volume case' rather than attributing an inference to the source. File.Replace's live Remarks state verbatim, 'If the sourceFileName and destinationFileName are on different volumes, this method raises an exception' — the article now quotes this exactly instead of the fabricated 'must be on the same drive.' I also re-ran a fresh full read of the entire article and re-verified, directly against live pages, the NTFS MFT quotes ('There is at least one entry in the MFT for every file...', the MFT-entries-vs-space-outside-the-MFT sentence) and the ifork.html extent-tree quote (the 1,000-block / ee_len=1000 comparison) — both exact, unchanged from round 1's already-thorough check. Code: all four run blocks pass 3/3 identical (blocks=8, executed=4), consistent with round 1's independent standalone dotnet-run verification, and nothing in this round touched the code blocks. Structure, honesty about the Windows-vs-Linux verification boundary, the exercises, and the diagrams are all unchanged from round 1's assessment and remain sound. One new, minor finding: the blockgroup.html quote itself has a tiny fidelity slip. The source's actual sentence is 'It is continuous range of blocks large enough to contain...' (grammatically missing its own article, apparently a typo in the kernel docs), but the article renders the quoted fragment as 'a continuous range of blocks large enough to contain...' — inserting the word 'a' inside quotation marks that the cited page does not contain. The underlying fact is accurate and the insertion doesn't change the meaning (if anything it repairs the source's own grammar), so this doesn't rise to the level of round 1's 'real'-for-'slow' substitution, which changed the sentence's actual content. It's a nit, not a blocker, but a quotation in quotation marks should be byte-for-byte or not be presented as a quotation at all. This keeps the score just under a clean 9.5+: an otherwise exemplary, rigorously sourced revision with one leftover word-level quote-fidelity slip.
